summary: Race-condition fix on PUT /api/pros-cons/{id}/assessments/{oid}/{fid} VERIFIED via dedicated concurrency test. Backend now uses MongoDB nested $set per field — concurrent partial PUTs (actual_value + assessment_pct flushed in parallel by DebouncedInput) BOTH survive consistently across 5 race-runs and a 3-way (actual+pct+satisfaction) variant. HOWEVER: the original fix contained a CRITICAL regression that I had to repair — line 731 of pros_cons.py used projection `{'factors.$': 1}` without a positional filter on the factors array, causing every PUT to fail with `pymongo.errors.OperationFailure: positional operator '.$' couldn't find a matching element`. Removed the bogus projection (the `factor` is already in scope from _load_analysis above) — Step 7 cell persistence is now fully functional. SWOT mirror at /app/backend/routes/swot.py was already correct (no projection bug). Issue #1 (auto-ladder) and Issue #2 (std_gap) regression checks still PASS.

critical_code_review_comments: When using `find_one` with a positional projection like `'factors.$': 1`, the FILTER must include an array-element match (e.g. `{'factors.id': factor_id}`). Otherwise MongoDB rejects with OperationFailure 51246. This was a latent bug in the original race fix that broke 100% of writes until repaired.

Defaults seeding inside upsert_assessment (lines 711-718) writes default values via `$set` for keys not present in the body — this is safe for first-time cell creation, but COULD theoretically race with a concurrent first-time write of a different field on a brand-new cell, leading to both writers seeding defaults. The current `existing_cell` snapshot check mitigates this for already-created cells; for the brand-new-cell race the worst case is just both writers attempting identical default-key $sets which is idempotent. Acceptable.

rca_of_issue: Race condition root cause (now fixed): old _persist() did read-modify-write of full assessments dict, so two parallel handlers each loaded the same stale snapshot, applied their partial patch on top, and the later writer's full-dict write clobbered the earlier writer's field. New impl uses `db.pros_cons.update_one({...}, {'$set': {'assessments.{oid}.{fid}.actual_value': '55000'}})` for ONLY the keys in the body — MongoDB merges the $set into the existing nested doc, so two parallel $sets touching different leaf keys cannot collide. The derived fields (cell_value, satisfaction_value) are computed after a re-read post-$set and written with their own atomic $set — even if a concurrent writer lands between read and derive-write, the derived values reflect the merged truth (which is what the UI shows on next GET). Verified by 5 consecutive race-runs all preserving both fields. Repair note: the original fix shipped with a broken find_one projection `{'factors.$': 1}` that 500'd every write; I removed it (factor already loaded earlier in the handler).
